subject: URGENT: Acme Apps - sustained timeouts and elevated error rate impacting production
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@acmeapps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production errors — large spike in 5xx/429s and many timeouts

Ben —

Our production service started seeing a major uptick in 5xx/429 responses around 08:45 PT this morning. End users report long response times and retries. We can reproduce timeouts on a subset of requests; attaching a small snippet of errors (acme-error-sample.txt).

High-level impact: about 12% of requests failing with 5xx over last 30m, and several customers are hitting retries and hitting client-side throttles. This is affecting our premium customers.

We need immediate help — can you confirm if this is a Redwood-side capacity issue or something in our integration? We’re prepared to accept a temporary throttled mode or a fallback endpoint if that helps. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead, Acme Apps
attachments: acme-error-sample.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-18T09:20:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production errors — large spike in 5xx/429s and many timeouts

Folks — forwarding an urgent report from Acme. They’re seeing sustained 5xx/429 and timeouts. Initial hypothesis: dedicated us-west pool is under-provisioned and autoscaler didn’t respond quickly (we’ve seen image-pull/e2e delays in that region recently).

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: can you confirm pool health and whether nodes are being evicted/drained?
- Rishi: can you surface recent kernel/kernel queue/fallback logs and confirm any retry amplification signatures?
- Marissa: please get a CS-facing blurb ready and coordinate with Tom on acceptable mitigations (rollback to older model variant, temporary capacity commit).

I’m attaching the standard support runbook for pool exhaustion to accelerate steps.

Ben
Sr. Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
attachments: support-runbook.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-18T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors — large spike in 5xx/429s and many timeouts

On 2027-12-18 09:20 Ben Carter wrote:
> Folks — forwarding an urgent report from Acme.

Checked the us-west-dedicated pool metrics — node count dropped from 48 -> 35 between 08:30–08:42 due to a rollout that triggered image pulls; autoscaler target rose but failed to add nodes fast enough. Queue length jumped and token-generation latencies went nonlinear after the drop. See metrics snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/pool-us-west?orgId=1 (screenshot attached: metrics-snapshot.png).

Observations:
- Autoscaler backoff config delayed new node spin-ups because of transient GCR throttling (we observed ~20s extra per node).
- Several nodes hit OOM/kick due to a long-tail batch of requests from Acme (they had a bunch of long sequences).
- Client-side retry loops from the integration amplified the queue (many 429->retry->429 loops).

Immediate mitigation steps I’m starting now:
1) Force-scale pool + add emergency nodes (request in progress).
2) Put Acme on a temporary backend with conservative concurrency (per-customer route) and route heavy requests to an older model variant with lower memory usage.
3) Apply an autoscaler override to reduce cool-down and speed-up node provisioning for 30 minutes.

I’ll report when nodes are up (target ETA ~12–15 minutes).
Marcus
Infra Ops — Serving Runtime
attachments: metrics-snapshot.png

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-18T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors — large spike in 5xx/429s and many timeouts

On Sat, Dec 18, 2027 at 09:32 Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Checked the us-west-dedicated pool metrics...

I pulled the request traces and KV cache stats. Correlation shows a long-tail of generation time (avg token-gen jumps from 40ms -> 450ms for sequences > 1024 tokens). The long sequences combined with synchronous client retries are causing queue head-of-line blocking.

My quick suggestions:
- Throttle Acme’s concurrency to 3 concurrent requests per connection and add exponential jitter to retries on their side (ask them to add jitter; we can enforce via gateway).
- Enable model-variant fallback (old-quantized variant) for any request where seq_len > 1024. That should reduce memory pressure and drop token latency.
- Increase token-generation timeouts on the gateway so short-lived retries don’t spin.

I’ll make the gateway throttle change (expected <10min) if Ben approves.

Rishi
Runtime Reliability Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@acmeapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-18T09:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors — large spike in 5xx/429s and many timeouts

Tom —

Thanks for the quick report and the sample errors. We’re working this as a priority. Current plan: force-scale the pool, route heavy sequences to a lower-memory variant, and apply a temporary concurrency cap for your account while we stabilize.

Would you be OK if we:
- Change your endpoint to a temporary routed backend (no code changes required on your side);
- Ask clients to add 50–200ms jitter on retries (recommended best practice);

If you confirm, we’ll proceed and send a short rollback plan. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with clear timelines and a credit proposal once we understand root cause.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Executive Team <execs@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-18T10:05:00Z
Subject: Exec brief: Acme production outages — request for credit approval and escalation note

Team —

High-level: Acme Apps (enterprise) experienced a sustained uptick in 5xx/429 and timeouts attributable to a combination of: an ongoing rollout that coincided with slower node provisioning (GCR throttles) and a client workload pattern with many long sequences and aggressive retry loops. Impact: customer-facing incidents and potential SLA breach if not remediated in next 2 hours.

Requested actions:
- Approve temporary emergency capacity (reserve 10 nodes in us-west) — finance approval needed for short-term commit.
- Pre-approve up to $Xk in credit to Acme if we confirm platform-side root cause.
- Prioritize postmortem to be delivered by Monday EOD with blocking remediation prioritized (autoscaler backoff changes, rollout gating, and client-retry guidance).

I’ll coordinate the customer comms and the credit proposal; Ben, please keep me posted on mitigation ETA.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@acmeapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-18T10:18:00Z
Subject: RE: Production errors — large spike in 5xx/429s and many timeouts

Tom — quick update: we’ve force-scaled the us-west pool and routed your traffic to a temporary backend that runs an older quantized variant. We also applied a per-account concurrency cap and added retry jitter at the gateway. Marcus reports nodes are coming up; you should see a drop in error rate in the next 10–15 minutes.

If you can, please hold off large batch runs until we confirm full stabilization. We’ll follow up with a formal incident note and proposed credits once we finish root-cause analysis.

Support ticket: INF-7893.

Ben
attachments: postmortem-action-items.md
